item.title: Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from 1994
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at West Norfolk headlines from 1994
We are looking back at the stories making headlines in West Norfolk during 1994. Plans for a two-million-pound science and technology block at Norfolk College in King’s Lynn were sent back to the drawing board after planners refused to allow protected trees to be removed. Meanwhile, the St Augustine’s Sports and Social Club in North Lynn celebrated its 21st birthday with a party for 350 members.
Elsewhere that year, Fakenham councillors raised concerns over the relocation of the town’s post office, while Lynnsport hosted a major careers convention. Additionally, Middleton Village Hall announced early plans for VE-Day anniversary celebrations, and the local NHS trust reported that hospital waiting times had been successfully reduced.

item.title: Major investment programme begins for Fenland play areas
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Major investment programme begins for Fenland play areas
Work has started on a wide-ranging project to upgrade play areas across the Fens. Fenland District Council is using £1.5 million in government funding, alongside a further £240,000 specifically for Wisbech, to improve facilities following public consultation.
Improvements are underway in Chatteris, March, Whittlesey, and Wisbech, with additional work planned for several villages including Tydd St Giles and Manea. Projects range from new play equipment and lighting to improved seating and landscaping. While some sites are already being transformed, others require planning permission or contractor tendering. Most schemes are expected to be completed by the end of 2027, with some specific playground projects continuing into 2028.
